title: Best USD Accounts for UK Residents: 7 Options Compared | Grey
summary: The 7 best ways to get a US dollar account in the UK. Options for residents and non-residents, with fees and requirements compared. Open yours now.
body_markdown:
If you earn in US dollars, pay for USD-billed services regularly, or do business with American clients, having a USD account as a UK resident makes practical and financial sense. Converting every dollar payment to sterling on arrival, at your bank’s rate, costs money every time. A USD account lets you hold the dollars, spend from them, and convert only what you need, when you need it.


The options available to UK residents vary significantly: some provide real US banking details that allow ACH payments from American clients, others hold USD but only receive via SWIFT, and a few have minimum balance requirements that make them unsuitable for most freelancers and remote workers.


This guide covers the seven best USD accounts for UK residents with verified fees and honest limitations for each, so you can find the one that suits your specific situation. For a fuller overview of opening USD accounts as a UK resident, see our[full guide to opening a USD account in the UK](https://grey.co/blog/best-banks-for-non-residents-to-open-uk-and-us-accounts) . For what a foreign currency account actually is, see our explainer on[what a foreign currency account](https://grey.co/blog/getting-your-foreign-currency-account) is.


## What to look for in a USD account as a UK resident


Usually, the most important thing to look out for is whether the account provides a real[US routing number](https://grey.co/blog/swift-code-vs-routing-number) and account number, or only receives USD via SWIFT.


A real US routing number and account number let US clients and employers pay you via ACH, the standard US domestic payment method. ACH is free or near-free for the sender, arrives in one to two business days, and requires no manual international wire process. If your account only receives USD via SWIFT, US senders must initiate an international wire, which costs $25 to $50 to send and may incur additional funds for correspondent bank deductions in transit.


Beyond ACH capability, four other things that are important in deciding factors are: whether there is a USD debit card for spending, what the monthly account fee is, what the USD-to-GBP conversion spread is when you do need to convert, and whether the account can be opened without an existing banking relationship or a high minimum balance.


## The 7 best USD accounts for UK residents


### 1. Grey


Grey provides UK residents with a full USD account backed by a real US routing number, account number, and SWIFT code, issued through Grey's US partner bank infrastructure. US clients pay via ACH, the standard domestic transfer method. The full amount arrives in your Grey USD balance in one to two business days, with no correspondent bank deductions.


**Key features:**


- US routing number and account number for ACH receipt
- SWIFT code for international wire receipt
- No monthly maintenance fee
- [Virtual USD card](https://grey.co/cards) for spending on USD-billed platforms
- Multi-currency: also provides EUR IBAN and GBP sort code and account number
- Conversion fee: 1% capped at $6
- Deposit fee via ACH: 0.8%, capped at $10


**Fees:** No monthly fee. Deposit fee 0.8% (min $2, max $10). Conversion 1% capped at $6. Virtual card creation is $5.


**Best for:** UK-based freelancers and remote workers receiving regular USD payments from US clients, and anyone who wants to receive details in EUR and GBP from a single account.


[Open a Grey USD account](https://grey.co/foreign-accounts)


### 2. Wise


Wise provides UK residents with a USD account that includes both an ACH routing number and a wire routing number, as well as a linked Wise debit card. ACH receipt is free, while receiving a domestic wire costs $6.11. Wise generally uses the mid-market rate for all conversions and charges a transparent flat fee, typically 0.43 to 0.57% of the converted amount, making it one of the cheapest options for USD-to-GBP conversion.


**Key features:**


- Real US ACH routing number and wire routing number
- ACH receipt: free
- Domestic wire receipt: $6.11
- Wise debit card available (Wise card; check availability for UK accounts)
- Conversion: mid-market rate plus flat fee from ~0.43%
- 40+ currencies supported
- No monthly fee


**Fees:** No monthly fee. ACH receipt is free. Wire receipt costs $6.11. Conversion charge is about 0.43% of the amount.


**Best for:** UK freelancers and remote workers who want the lowest USD-to-GBP conversion margin and a wide multi-currency account. Strong choice alongside Grey for those who need to convert regularly.


### 3. Revolut


Revolut’s situation for UK personal account holders requires an important clarification. Revolut UK personal accounts receive USD via SWIFT rather than via US local ACH, so US clients cannot pay via standard domestic ACH transfers. This matters for freelancers: US clients paying via SWIFT face a $25 to $50 outbound wire fee, and the transfer takes three to five business days rather than one to two.


Revolut does provide USD accounts with local US ACH details to US-registered users and to UK business users with US incorporation. For most UK personal account holders, however, Revolut’s USD account is a currency holding and SWIFT receipt account rather than a true ACH-capable US account.


Standard plan holders can exchange up to £1,000 per month for free, with a 1% fair usage fee above that.


**Key features:**


- USD currency account available for UK personal and business customers
- UK personal accounts: USD received via SWIFT only, not ACH
- Revolut debit card for spending in USD
- Standard plan: no monthly fee, £1,000/month free exchange
- Premium plan: £7.99/month, £3,000/month free exchange
- Exchange above monthly limit: 0.5% fair usage fee


**Fees:** Standard plan: free. Premium: £7.99/month. Exchange: free within monthly limit, 0.5% above.


**Best for:** UK residents who want to hold and spend USD with a card and are comfortable receiving via SWIFT, or businesses with US incorporation needing ACH capability.


### 4. Barclays foreign currency account


Barclays offers USD accounts to both personal and business customers through its foreign currency account product. For personal customers, USD accounts are available through Barclays International Banking, which requires holding a minimum of £100,000 with Barclays to qualify. This makes it inaccessible for most freelancers and early-stage remote workers.


For business customers, Barclays offers a foreign currency account without the minimum balance requirement that applies to existing business banking customers. No debit card is issued with the foreign currency account, which limits its use for day-to-day USD spending.


**Key features:**


- USD account available for existing Barclays customers
- Personal: minimum £100,000 balance requirement for Barclays International Banking
- Business: available to existing business customers without the same minimum requirements
- No debit card issued with a foreign currency account
- SWIFT wire receipt
- Transfers between Barclays accounts are fee-free


**Fees:** Varies by account type.


**Best for:** Existing Barclays business customers who need a USD holding account for international trade and already have a Barclays business relationship.


#### 5. HSBC Expat (Jersey)


HSBC Expat, based in Jersey, provides multi-currency accounts including USD to UK residents and expatriates. It supports around 19 currencies, including GBP, USD, and EUR, and is designed for internationally mobile clients who want a relationship-based banking experience with a dedicated account manager.


The trade-off is the high minimum balance requirement and fees. HSBC Expat expects significant deposits or salary thresholds and applies an exchange adjustment of approximately 2.75% to non-sterling card payments and withdrawals. This makes regular USD-to-GBP conversion expensive compared to fintech alternatives.


**Key features:**


- 19 currencies supported, including USD
- Relationship manager and personal service
- Fee-free global transfers under qualifying conditions
- ~2.75% exchange adjustment on non-sterling card use
- High balance or salary thresholds to qualify
- SWIFT wire receipt


**Fees:** Monthly fees apply depending on the account package; minimum balance thresholds are required. Verify current requirements directly with HSBC Expat.


**Best for:** High-net-worth UK residents and expats who want a relationship banking experience, personal service, and multi-currency management alongside significant GBP and USD balances.


#### 6. Citibank UK


Citibank UK offers international banking services to UK residents, including USD accounts. Citibank’s global network is one of its primary advantages: clients can access accounts and services across Citibank’s international presence, which is useful for those who live and work across multiple countries.


Citibank UK’s private banking and international personal banking services are positioned for higher-income clients. Eligibility requirements and minimum balance thresholds apply, making it less accessible for freelancers or remote workers with moderate USD income.


**Key features:**


- USD accounts available alongside GBP and other currencies
- Global account access via Citibank’s international network
- Relationship banking with dedicated support
- SWIFT wire receipt for international payments
- Minimum balance and income thresholds apply


**Fees:** Varies by product tier. Contact Citibank UK directly for current eligibility and fee requirements.


**Best for:** UK residents with significant international banking needs who want a global bank with multi-country account access and are comfortable meeting higher eligibility thresholds.


#### 7. Starling Business (USD add-on)


Starling Bank offers a USD account add-on for existing Starling business account holders. The USD account costs £5 per month and allows business customers to hold and receive USD alongside their GBP business account. Note that at the time of research, Starling has paused issuing new USD accounts: check directly with Starling before applying, as availability may have changed.


The Starling USD account does not provide local US ACH routing numbers. USD receipts come in via SWIFT rather than ACH. It is also only available to businesses with a registered UK entity, not to sole traders.


**Key features:**


- USD account add-on for Starling Business account holders
- £5 per month
- Requires an existing GBP Starling Business account
- Available to registered UK businesses, not sole traders
- SWIFT wire receipt, not ACH
- No local US routing number


**Fees:** £5 per month for the USD add-on, plus the Starling Business account fee.


**Best for:** UK-registered businesses that already use Starling for their GBP operations and want a simple USD holding account alongside it, with ACH not required.


### Which USD account is best for UK freelancers?


For UK freelancers earning USD from US clients, the single most important feature is a real US ACH routing number and account number. Without one, your US client must send an international wire, which costs them $25 to $50 and takes three to five business days. With one, they[pay via ACH](https://grey.co/blog/wire-transfer-vs-ach-cheapest-way-to-receive-usd) as if you were a US-based vendor: free, fast, and fully automated in their accounting system.


Of the seven options above, only[Grey](https://grey.co/) and Wise provide UK residents with full US ACH routing details as personal account holders. Revolut UK personal accounts receive USD via SWIFT only, which defeats the purpose for freelancers billing US clients. Traditional banks (Barclays, HSBC, Citibank) have minimum balance requirements or relationship thresholds that make them inaccessible for most freelancers.


Between Grey and Wise, both are strong options. Grey's fee caps (deposit capped at $10, conversion capped at $6) make it more cost-effective for larger individual payments. Wise’s lower percentage conversion fee (0.43%) makes it cheaper for smaller, more frequent conversions. Many UK freelancers use both.


For a fuller picture of how to get paid by clients based in the US, see our guide on[how UK freelancers get paid by overseas clients](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-get-paid-by-overseas-clients-as-a-freelancer-in-the-uk) . If you also work with European clients, our piece on[how to open a euro account in the UK](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-send-and-receive-euros-in-the-uk) covers the EUR equivalent of this comparison.


[Open a Grey account](http://www.onelink.to/grey) and get a real USD account number and routing number in minutes, from anywhere in the UK.


### Frequently asked questions


### **Can I get a real US bank account as a UK resident?**


Yes. Grey and Wise both provide UK residents with real US account numbers and ACH routing numbers without requiring a US address, US entity, or a visit to the US. These accounts function like domestic US bank accounts for payment purposes: US clients and employers can pay via ACH as a standard domestic transfer. Traditional US banks generally require a US address and in-person opening, which makes them inaccessible to most UK residents.


### **Which is better, Wise or Grey, for a USD account?**


Both provide real ACH routing details and are the strongest options for UK freelancers receiving USD from US clients. Wise charges a conversion fee of approximately 0.43% of the amount, with no cap, using the mid-market rate. Grey charges a 0.8% deposit fee, capped at $10, and a 1% conversion fee, capped at $6. For smaller, frequent conversions, Wise’s lower percentage rate is cheaper. For larger individual payments above approximately $1,000, Grey's fee caps mean a lower total cost. Many users hold both accounts.


### **Does Revolut give UK residents a real USD account number?**


Revolut UK personal accounts offer USD accounts, but inbound USD payments for UK account holders are received via SWIFT rather than via local US ACH. This means US clients cannot pay via standard ACH transfer and must send an international wire instead. Revolut Business accounts with US incorporation can access local US ACH details. For UK personal account holders who need ACH capability, Grey or Wise are the more suitable options.


### **Can I receive ACH payments into a UK USD account?**


Yes, if the account provides real US ACH routing details. Grey and Wise both provide UK residents with ACH routing numbers and US account numbers that accept domestic ACH payments from US senders. Revolut UK personal accounts, Barclays foreign currency accounts, and Starling USD business accounts do not provide local US ACH details and receive USD only via SWIFT.


### **What is the cheapest USD account for UK residents?**


For no monthly fee and low conversion costs, Grey and Wise are both strong options. Grey has no monthly fee, charges 0.8% on deposits capped at $10, and 1% on conversion capped at $6. Wise has no monthly fee, charges nothing to receive via ACH, and converts at approximately 0.43% above the mid-market rate. Revolut’s Standard plan is free but has monthly exchange limits of £1,000 before a 0.5% fair usage fee applies, and UK personal accounts don’t provide ACH details. Traditional bank USD accounts (Barclays, HSBC, Citibank) tend to have higher fees and minimum balance requirements.
